biography: Fábio Ebrahim's journey began not on the asphalt, but on the dusty dirt tracks of his family's farm in rural Brazil. Speed was in his blood, inherited from a grandfather who raced stock cars on weekends. He traded tractors for karts as a teenager, quickly dominating the local scene with a raw, untamed style. After winning the Brazilian Karting Championship, Fábio made the jump to open-wheel racing. The transition wasn't seamless; a few costly crashes threatened to derail his career before it truly began. However, a pivotal win at Interlagos in the Formula Brazil series caught the eye of Ginetta, who offered him a spot in their GT program. He’s now a seasoned racer, known for his relentless pursuit of victory, currently driving for Ginetta and considered to be in his prime.
drivingStyle: Ebrahim is an aggressive, late-braking driver known for his daring overtakes. He's not afraid to push the limits of his car and the track, often threading the needle in situations where others would back off. Tire management isn't his strongest suit; he tends to overdrive the car early in a stint, sacrificing long-run pace for immediate gains. Under pressure, he can be prone to errors, but his unwavering determination often sees him claw back lost ground.

rivalries.name: Marco Silva
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days, fueled by several on-track collisions and accusations of unfair tactics.

rivalries.name: Isabella Rossi
rivalries.reason: A fierce competitor who challenges Ebrahim's aggressive style with her own calculated precision, leading to numerous close battles and heated exchanges.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A rivalry born from a controversial incident at Suzuka, where Ebrahim's aggressive move forced Tanaka off the track, costing him a potential podium finish.

quirks: Always wears a lucky pair of socks with a pattern of miniature racing flags.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song moments before getting into the car.
Refuses to shave on race weekends, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Spa in 2020, driving a Ginetta, after an epic final-lap battle against a heavily favored Porsche team.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 2018 Brazilian Grand Prix with only two laps remaining, handing the victory to his arch-rival, Marco Silva.
